captions.text: Recap of chapter 00: you installed Python, the language for this whole course.
You installed Ollama, which runs AI models on your own computer.
You downloaded a model and talked to it.
The setup check passed. Now you'll learn the Python you need.
Today's black box: how a Python program works.
Let's open it.
A program is a text file of instructions. Python runs them from top to bottom.
A variable is a name for a value. Equals stores the value under that name.
Each value has a type: text, a whole number, or true and false.
An f-string puts values inside text. Put them in curly brackets.
if runs code only when a condition is true. Python uses the first match.
The four spaces matter. Indentation shows which lines belong to the if.
A for loop repeats for each value. range(1, 4) stops before 4.
A while loop repeats while a condition is true, so it must change eventually.
A function is a named block of code you can reuse.
Parameters are its inputs, and return sends a result back.
Call a function by name, and pass in values.
Later, an agent's tools will be ordinary functions just like these.
Now run it. The output comes from top to bottom.
The decision picks one result, and the loops repeat.
The last line came from your two functions.
Errors are normal. Read the last line first.
Python can't add text and a number. An f-string fixes this.
Your turn. Open exercises.py and complete the five TODOs.
You've finished when you see 5/5 passed.
